**Source 1:** World Health Organization (WHO), "COVID-19 Mythbusters: Fact or Fiction", no specific original date shown [1]. The WHO states that there is no scientific evidence showing that lemon or household remedies prevent or cure COVID-19, nor does drinking water flush out or kill the virus [1]. (Claim c1)

**Source 2:** National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, "Lemon juice will not prevent or cure a COVID-19 infection, no matter what is mixed with it", published April 22, 2020 [2]. The advisory notes that acidic drinks like lemon juice do not destroy the novel coronavirus inside human cells, and drinking hot lemon juice does not stop the virus or prevent infection [2]. (Claim c1)

**Source 3:** AFP Fact Check, "False claims that drinking water with lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online", published March 12, 2020 [3]. Medical experts told AFP that claims suggesting hot or lukewarm water with lemon slices can prevent or kill the virus are false, as consuming lemon provides no proven therapeutic effect against SARS-CoV-2 [3]. (Claim c1)

**Source 4:** FactCheck.org, "Lemon Juice Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel, or Anywhere Else", published April 2, 2020 [4]. Infectious disease specialists confirmed there is no clinical data indicating that lemon juice or hot beverages kill coronavirus in the body [4]. (Claim c1)

**Source 5:** NDTV Food / PIB Fact Check, "Can Lemon And Hot Water Kill Coronavirus? Experts Bust Popular Myths", published May 5, 2021 [5]. The report highlights fact-checks by the Indian government's Press Information Bureau (PIB) clarifying that viral messages claiming hot water mixed with lemon kills or eliminates COVID-19 are fake and lack scientific backing [5]. (Claim c1)

**Source 6:** Alt News Science, "No, Vitamin C and lemon-infused hot water do not protect against coronavirus or cancer", published March 18, 2020 [6]. The fact-check debunked viral messages regarding lemon slices in warm water, confirming there is no evidence that lemon water destroys the coronavirus [6]. (Claim c1)
